title: DROP SCHEMA
description: Learn how to remove a schema from a database using DROP SCHEMA.

data.text: The DROP SCHEMA statement removes a schema from a database. The schema must be empty before it can be dropped.

data.title: DROP SCHEMA Syntax
data.content: Drops a schema if it exists.

data.text: If the schema contains any objects, the statement will fail. You must delete all objects in the schema before removing it.
The following example creates a logistics schema, adds a table, then attempts to drop the schema.

data.title: Create and Drop Schema
data.content: Creates logistics schema with a table, then drops both.

data.text: SQL Server issues an error because the schema is not empty:

data.title: Error: Schema Not Empty
data.content: Error message when trying to drop a non-empty schema.
data.code:
Msg 3729, Level 16, State 1, Line 1
Cannot drop schema 'logistics' because it is being referenced by object 'deliveries'.

data.text: First drop the table, then drop the schema:

data.title: Drop Table Then Schema
data.content: Drops the deliveries table first, then the logistics schema.
data.code:
DROP TABLE logistics.deliveries;

DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS logistics;

data.title: DROP SCHEMA Key Points
points: Use DROP SCHEMA to remove a schema from a database.
The schema must be empty before it can be dropped.
Use IF EXISTS to avoid errors for non-existent schemas.
Drop all objects in the schema before dropping the schema itself.
